title: Go
philosophy: Simplicity as a feature — a small language you can hold in your head, moving fast on concepts you already own while learning the explicit, boring-on-purpose style that powers real servers and tools.

units.title: Go Fast Foundations
units.summary: Compressed basics; assumes any prior track's Foundations but stands alone.

units.title: Methods and Interfaces
units.summary: How Go does objects: methods on types and small, implicit interfaces.

units.title: Errors the Go Way
units.summary: Errors as values — the idiom that defines Go code; ends with the Core capstone.
topics: errors are values: the (T, error) pattern
panic and recover — and why you rarely use them

units.title: Packages and Modules
units.summary: Organizing real projects: packages, modules, and dependencies.

units.title: Concurrency
units.summary: Goroutines and channels — Go's crown jewel, given the room it deserves.
topics: goroutines and the scheduler mental model
mutexes and when channels aren't the answer

units.title: Standard Library in Practice
units.summary: The stdlib doing real work — files, JSON, HTTP both ways; ends with the Intermediate capstone.
topics: files with os, io, and bufio
net/http as a server: handlers and ServeMux
flag and os.Args for CLI tools

units.title: Testing and Tooling
units.summary: The toolchain as a superpower: tests, benchmarks, vet, and profiling.

units.title: Capstone: Small Web Service
units.summary: Multi-session capstone: a tested web service (or CLI), built like production.
topics: concurrency where it earns its keep
